targets.label: You do not have a Social Security number.

note: Check Box1 (T13) is Debtor 1's "You do not have a Social Security number." has_ssn_check returns "true" when the debtor HAS an SSN, so this logic is inverted. It is harmless today only because the emitted "/Yes" does not match on_state "On" (pypdf writes /Off). Fixing only on_states would falsely tell the court that every SSN-holder has no SSN. Having an SSN is shown by writing it in Debtor1a.SSNum, so this box stays blank.

produces: "true" if Debtor 1 has no SSN, else "" -> checkbox emits "/Yes"

targets.label: You do not have a Social Security number.

note: Check Box2 (T14) is the Debtor 2 column's "You do not have a Social Security number." no_ssn_check describes Debtor 1, so it belongs on Check Box1. It also never ticks: "/Yes" vs on_state "On".

No widget is named Debtor2a.First name; the real box is "Debtor2.First name" (T4), so nothing is written. Even if it were, rule first_name returns Debtor 1's first name, not the spouse's. Gated by has_joint_filer (latent: joint_filer_gate is never written).
The real box is "Debtor2.Middle name_2" (T6). The rule returns Debtor 1's middle name.
The real box is "Debtor2.Last name" (T8). The rule returns Debtor 1's last name.

produces: Debtor 1 SSN as NNN-NN-NNNN (11 chars) or "" [only when has_joint_filer]

targets.column: For Debtor 2 (Only If Spouse Is Filing):

note: The box is right: line 2, Debtor 2 column (T10). But ssn_formatted reads session.debtor_info.ssn, which is Debtor 1, so for a joint filer Debtor 1's full SSN is printed as the spouse's SSN. The co-debtor SSN entered in the wizard (co_debtor_ssn) is not stored at all, because DebtorInfo and its serializer have no such field. Gated by has_joint_filer (latent: joint_filer_gate is never written).

Short name "signature" matches Debtor1.signature (T21) and Debtor2.signature (T22), so a single filer's name also appears on the "Signature of Debtor 2" line. Typed full name (no '/s/') written into a wet-signature line.

The key matches "Executed on" (T23, Debtor 1 date) and, by short name, "Debtor2.Executed on" (T24). Short-name matching makes T23 impossible to address alone. today_iso writes 'YYYY-MM-DD'; the printed box asks MM/DD/YYYY (format only).
